gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the equipment has been serviced this year, so breakdowns are rare.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of + noun' = the majority of it; 'the most' is a superlative.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.
'Somewhere' is used in affirmative sentences; adjectives like 'quiet' follow the -where word.

gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.

gaps.sentence: ___ smells burnt in here — can you check the oven?
gaps.hint: affirmative statement about an unknown thing
gaps.explanation: 'Something' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown thing; the request to check the oven shows the speaker believes it.
